description: Attributed comparative index. These records are not Arcanea canon and are never projected to Starlight Memory.

entities.name: Raava
entities.namingObservation: Short invented proper name paired with a cosmological office.

usage.transferablePattern: A world-scale presence enters a durable relationship without making either party reducible to the other.

entities.name: Vaatu
entities.namingObservation: Short invented proper name designed as a counterpart.

usage.transferablePattern: A suppressed cosmological pressure returns cyclically and cannot be solved by permanent erasure.

entities.name: Tui
entities.namingObservation: Single-syllable name associated with a natural office.

usage.transferablePattern: A vast natural function becomes locally vulnerable by choosing a bounded embodiment.

entities.name: La
entities.namingObservation: Single-syllable name functioning as one half of a natural pair.

usage.transferablePattern: Interdependent natural offices generate motion through difference rather than hierarchy.

entities.name: Hei Bai
entities.namingObservation: Compact translated name built around contrast.

usage.transferablePattern: Damage to a place alters the form and behavior of the presence that carries its continuity.

entities.name: Koh
entities.namingObservation: Short proper name joined to a descriptive epithet in common use.

usage.transferablePattern: A dangerous encounter is governed by a precise behavioral constraint tied to identity.

entities.name: Wan Shi Tong
entities.namingObservation: Meaning-bearing Chinese-language title associated with an office.

usage.transferablePattern: Knowledge access is a negotiated civic and moral relationship, not a neutral inventory.

entities.name: Mother of Faces
entities.namingObservation: Relational title plus governed domain.

usage.transferablePattern: An identity-changing gift becomes ethically complex because appearance, memory, and relation diverge.

entities.name: Father Glowworm
entities.namingObservation: Kinship title combined with an animal-light image.

usage.transferablePattern: A gate-making presence turns passage into leverage and can be injured through the interface it opens.

entities.name: General Old Iron
entities.namingObservation: Military title plus material epithet.

usage.transferablePattern: A protector outlives the context of its war and must confront whether its grievance still serves the place.

entities.name: Lady Tienhai
entities.namingObservation: Honorific title plus personal name.

usage.transferablePattern: A presence becomes inseparable from a settlement through sacrifice, stewardship, and contested memory.

entities.name: Painted Lady
entities.namingObservation: Descriptive mantle rather than a disclosed personal name.

usage.transferablePattern: A community's protective mantle can be enacted by a human before the actual presence reappears.

entities.name: Aye-Aye Spirit
entities.namingObservation: Species-derived Common Sign with a class descriptor.

usage.transferablePattern: Hospitality develops through repeated conduct rather than destiny or automatic moral purity.

entities.name: Bum-Ju
entities.namingObservation: Short hyphenated invented name.

usage.transferablePattern: A small companion can carry emotional continuity without functioning as a combat upgrade.

entities.name: Dragon eel spirit
entities.namingObservation: Compound animal class name.

usage.transferablePattern: Movement through another realm can depend on negotiating with a mobile native presence.

entities.name: Knowledge Seekers
entities.namingObservation: Collective named directly for its function.

usage.transferablePattern: A knowledge institution can be maintained by a distributed nonhuman workforce with its own agenda.

entities.name: Kemurikage
entities.namingObservation: Japanese-language coined collective name.

usage.transferablePattern: A feared historical image can be imitated by humans and gain power through social expectation.

entities.name: Fog of Lost Souls
entities.namingObservation: Descriptive location-phenomenon title.

usage.transferablePattern: A place can trap inhabitants inside self-reinforcing memory without being a conventional villain.

entities.name: Tree of Time
entities.namingObservation: Archetypal object-plus-domain title.

usage.transferablePattern: A site can store world-scale temporal relation without behaving as an owned database.

entities.name: Dark spirits
entities.namingObservation: State label applied across many otherwise distinct entities.

usage.transferablePattern: A spirit's visible and behavioral state can change through imbalance without defining its permanent essence.

entities.name: Haku / Kohaku River spirit
entities.namingObservation: Personal abbreviation conceals a longer place-linked identity.

usage.transferablePattern: Recovering a place-linked name can restore agency and continuity after displacement.

entities.name: No-Face
entities.namingObservation: Absence-based descriptive Common Sign.

usage.transferablePattern: An ambiguous presence absorbs the appetite and behavior of the institution that hosts it.

entities.name: River Spirit
entities.namingObservation: Natural office used in place of an individual name.

usage.transferablePattern: Pollution changes how a place-person is perceived, and communal labor can reveal rather than create its dignity.

entities.name: Radish Spirit
entities.namingObservation: Plant-office descriptive Common Sign.

usage.transferablePattern: Minor spirits can establish a lived society through ordinary courtesy rather than exposition.

entities.name: Forest Spirit
entities.namingObservation: Place-domain office without a personal Common Sign.

usage.transferablePattern: Creation and death can belong to one ecological office whose embodiment makes the forest politically vulnerable.

entities.name: Kodama
entities.namingObservation: Borrowed Japanese folkloric class term.

usage.transferablePattern: The presence or absence of small distributed beings makes ecosystem health visible.

entities.name: Totoro
entities.namingObservation: Invented child-spoken proper name.

usage.transferablePattern: Perception and trust can be situational without making the presence imaginary or universally visible.

entities.name: Susuwatari
entities.namingObservation: Japanese coined class name translated variously across editions.

usage.transferablePattern: A place's hidden maintenance can be personified as a small collective with appetite and labor conditions.

entities.name: Amidamaru
entities.namingObservation: Japanese personal name retained across a long partnership.

usage.transferablePattern: A dead expert and living partner build capability through trust, medium, and repeated co-action.

entities.name: Matamune
entities.namingObservation: Short Japanese proper name.

usage.transferablePattern: A mentor's finite continuity can be spent in a way that creates inheritance and grief rather than reusable power.

entities.name: Spirit of Fire
entities.namingObservation: Elemental office stated as a title.

usage.transferablePattern: A vast elemental partner has its own growth mechanics and cannot be treated as an inert spell slot.

entities.name: Great Spirit
entities.namingObservation: Scale adjective plus generic spiritual office.

usage.transferablePattern: World memory and rulership can be linked through an office whose succession creates political stakes.

entities.name: Zanpakutō spirits
entities.namingObservation: Japanese weapon-class term with each individual carrying a distinct name.

usage.transferablePattern: A weapon's full capability depends on relationship with an agentive inner counterpart rather than ownership alone.

entities.name: Hollows
entities.namingObservation: English absence-state class term.

usage.transferablePattern: Unresolved continuity can become predatory through progressive identity loss while retaining a path to transformation.

entities.name: Pluses
entities.namingObservation: Abstract positive-sign term for a soul state.

usage.transferablePattern: Attachment can delay transition without making the dead automatically malicious.

entities.name: Madara / Nyanko-sensei
entities.namingObservation: A personal name and comic social nickname coexist across forms.

usage.transferablePattern: A protector's self-interest, affection, and changing forms can coexist without reducing the relationship to purity.

entities.name: Hinoe
entities.namingObservation: Japanese personal name rather than a species descriptor.

usage.transferablePattern: A spirit can relate differently to successive generations while retaining history and preference.

entities.name: Book of Friends name bonds
entities.namingObservation: Friendly title conceals a coercive registry function.

usage.transferablePattern: A descendant can inherit responsibility to release names without inheriting moral ownership of the bound beings.

entities.name: Mushi
entities.namingObservation: Short Japanese class term deliberately broader than ordinary animals.

usage.transferablePattern: Strange beings can be ecological conditions with consequences rather than villains, pets, or gods.

entities.name: Cursed spirits
entities.namingObservation: State-plus-class term describes origin and threat.

usage.transferablePattern: Repeated collective emotion can condense into agentive pressure that outlives any single contributor.

entities.name: Loose spirits
entities.namingObservation: Condition descriptor precedes assignment to a divine relationship.

usage.transferablePattern: Unresolved dead-person continuity becomes vulnerable to institutions that assign names and roles.

entities.name: Shinki
entities.namingObservation: Japanese office term; individuals receive names from a god.

usage.transferablePattern: A bond can make each party vulnerable to the other's conduct, exposing the ethics of naming and weaponization.

entities.name: Heroic Spirits / Servants
entities.namingObservation: Office and container terms distinguish stored identity from summoned instance.

usage.transferablePattern: A culturally remembered figure can manifest only partially through a constrained local vessel.

entities.name: Celestial Spirits
entities.namingObservation: Domain adjective plus generic class; many names derive from constellations.

usage.transferablePattern: Summoned allies can have schedules, rights, relationships, and a home polity beyond the summoner.

entities.name: Elemental Spirits
entities.namingObservation: Generic elemental office with individual myth-derived names.

usage.transferablePattern: A rare elemental presence chooses a partner and develops through shared experience rather than being manufactured.

entities.name: Devils
entities.namingObservation: Entities are named directly for the feared concept they embody.

usage.transferablePattern: Social attention can strengthen a concept-person while contracts externalize price and asymmetry.

entities.name: Dimple
entities.namingObservation: Comic appearance-based nickname replaces a grand self-presentation.

usage.transferablePattern: A hostile spirit relationship can change through sustained interaction without erasing ambition or prior harm.

entities.name: Mononoke
entities.namingObservation: Japanese supernatural class term with culturally specific history.

usage.transferablePattern: Resolution requires understanding the presence's form, causal truth, and motive rather than applying force alone.

entities.name: Kami
entities.namingObservation: A broad Japanese term whose meaning changes by context, source, and practice.

usage.transferablePattern: Presence and relation may be more fundamental than a fixed fantasy-species taxonomy.

entities.name: Yōkai
entities.namingObservation: Japanese umbrella term with changing historical and popular meanings.

usage.transferablePattern: A culture's category for strangeness can organize stories without asserting one biological species.

entities.name: Yūrei
entities.namingObservation: Japanese dead-person spirit category with context-specific subtypes.

usage.transferablePattern: Claims of dead-person continuity can carry unresolved social obligation and require culturally situated repair.

entities.name: Tsukumogami
entities.namingObservation: Japanese category associated with old tools and later folklore/art traditions.

usage.transferablePattern: Long use and accumulated relation can make the disposal of an object ethically and narratively charged.

entities.name: Daimon
entities.namingObservation: Ancient Greek term with meanings that vary across authors and periods.

usage.transferablePattern: Unseen agency may be experienced as distributed power or office rather than a fixed creature species.

entities.name: Nymph
entities.namingObservation: Broad ancient category with place- and medium-specific groups.

usage.transferablePattern: A river, spring, tree, cave, or mountain can be socially encountered through a person-like local presence.

entities.name: Ka
entities.namingObservation: Transliterated Egyptian concept; not equivalent to a complete Western soul.

usage.transferablePattern: Personhood can be modeled as several relational continuities rather than one indivisible soul object.

entities.name: Ba
entities.namingObservation: Transliterated Egyptian concept with period-dependent meaning.

usage.transferablePattern: Mobility, personality, body, and post-death continuity may be distinct but interdependent functions.

entities.name: Akh
entities.namingObservation: Transliterated Egyptian term often glossed as an effective transformed spirit.

usage.transferablePattern: Post-death continuity may be an achieved transformation dependent on relation and practice rather than an automatic state.

entities.name: Ren
entities.namingObservation: Transliterated Egyptian concept associated with name and continued identity.

usage.transferablePattern: A publicly maintained name can be one component of continuity without becoming a command key.

entities.name: Sheut / shadow
entities.namingObservation: Transliterated term often translated as shadow; not Arcanea's Shadow corruption.

usage.transferablePattern: A shadow can be treated as one relational aspect of personhood without moralizing darkness.

entities.name: Fylgja
entities.namingObservation: Old Norse term with contested and source-dependent meanings.

usage.transferablePattern: A companion presence may externalize inherited character, fate, or relational identity without being a pet.

entities.name: Landvættir
entities.namingObservation: Old Norse plural term tied to land beings.

usage.transferablePattern: Political and ecological conduct toward land can be mediated through a plural local presence.

entities.name: Dísir
entities.namingObservation: Old Norse plural term with overlapping textual meanings.

usage.transferablePattern: Ancestral, protective, and fate-related functions may belong to a plural office rather than one named individual.

entities.name: Aos Sí
entities.namingObservation: Irish-language collective term; not equivalent to generic modern fairies.

usage.transferablePattern: A nonhuman people may share geography through protocols of respect, timing, and reciprocal boundary.

entities.name: Domovoi
entities.namingObservation: Regional Slavic terms and forms vary; this transliteration is not universal.

usage.transferablePattern: Domestic maintenance, inherited place, and family behavior can cohere as a household counterparty.

entities.name: Leshy
entities.namingObservation: Regional forest-spirit term with variable forms and stories.

usage.transferablePattern: A forest can defend its own scale and paths by disrupting human orientation.

entities.name: Rusalka
entities.namingObservation: Regional term whose water, field, seasonal, and dead-person associations vary.

usage.transferablePattern: A seasonal place-presence can carry unresolved death and social danger without one universal origin story.

entities.name: Shén
entities.namingObservation: Chinese term with multiple religious, philosophical, bodily, and everyday meanings.

usage.transferablePattern: Spirit, divinity, vitality, and office may overlap without collapsing into a fantasy species.

entities.name: Guǐ
entities.namingObservation: Chinese term with contextual meanings often oversimplified in English as ghost.

usage.transferablePattern: Neglected relationship, ritual, or memory can shape how dead-person continuity is socially encountered.

entities.name: Yāoguài
entities.namingObservation: Chinese literary and folk category with shifting meanings.

usage.transferablePattern: Long-lived animals, objects, or forces may acquire personhood that institutions then classify as dangerous.

entities.name: Dokkaebi
entities.namingObservation: Korean term with regional, historical, and media-dependent forms.

usage.transferablePattern: A strange counterparty can test greed, courage, hospitality, or wit through rule-bound play.

entities.name: Gwishin
entities.namingObservation: Korean ghost category with multiple subtypes and contexts.

usage.transferablePattern: A haunting can preserve a social wrong that living institutions refuse to acknowledge.

entities.name: Yaksha / Yakshi
entities.namingObservation: Sanskrit-derived terms used across distinct historical Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and local contexts.

usage.transferablePattern: A formidable local nature presence can be integrated into changing religious and civic roles without losing its earlier complexity.

entities.name: Nāga / Nāginī
entities.namingObservation: Terms span multiple South and Southeast Asian religious and cultural contexts.

usage.transferablePattern: Water, fertility, treasure, protection, and dangerous sovereignty can coexist in one nonhuman people.

entities.name: Òrìṣà
entities.namingObservation: Yorùbá living religious term with lineage- and community-specific knowledge.

usage.transferablePattern: Blocked from automated transfer; preserved only as a marker that divine force, personhood, community, and lineage require living-context interpretation.

entities.name: Apu
entities.namingObservation: Quechua title used in living Andean contexts; meanings vary by community.

usage.transferablePattern: Blocked from automated transfer; preserves the constraint that a landscape may be a living social counterparty rather than scenery.
